comments.body:
I checked #233 and did not find a linked parent/tracking issue or comments.

For this `/answer` run I’m staying in plan-only mode. Short version: yes, Sepo should support more credential shapes, but updating only [`resolve-provider.sh`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/actions/resolve-agent-provider/resolve-provider.sh#L39-L45) is not enough. The workflow also needs to pass those secrets into the runtime via [`resolve-agent-provider/action.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/actions/resolve-agent-provider/action.yml#L16-L23), [`run-agent-task/action.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/actions/run-agent-task/action.yml#L294-L302), and [`run.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/run.ts#L256-L273).

**Current Sepo Behavior**

- Auto-detects Codex only from `OPENAI_API_KEY`.
- Auto-detects Claude only from `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`.
- Explicit `AGENT_DEFAULT_PROVIDER=codex|claude` already works without matching repo secrets, mainly for self-hosted runners with local auth.
- Runtime only forwards `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` to the agent process.

**Claude Code Supported Auth/Env Setups**

Based on current official Claude Code docs:

- Claude.ai subscription auth: `/login` for Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise.
- CI subscription auth: `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, generated via `claude setup-token`.
- Direct Anthropic API key: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.
- Bearer/proxy auth: `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`.
- Dynamic credentials: `apiKeyHelper` plus optional `CLAUDE_CODE_API_KEY_HELPER_TTL_MS`.
- Enterprise/team managed settings: managed `settings.json`/policy layers, including server-managed and OS/MDM/file-based managed settings.
- Amazon Bedrock: `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1`, `AWS_REGION`, AWS SDK credential chain or `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK`.
- Claude Platform on AWS: `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_ANTHROPIC_AWS=1`, `ANTHROPIC_AWS_WORKSPACE_ID`, `AWS_REGION`, plus AWS credentials or `ANTHROPIC_AWS_API_KEY`.
- Google Vertex AI: `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX=1`, `CLOUD_ML_REGION`, `ANTHROPIC_VERTEX_PROJECT_ID`, plus ADC / `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`.
- Microsoft Foundry/Azure: `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY=1`, `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_RESOURCE` or `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_BASE_URL`, plus `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_API_KEY` or Azure default credentials.
- LLM gateways/proxies: `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, optional `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS`, gateway model discovery flags.

Sources: [Claude auth](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication), [Claude env vars](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars), [Bedrock](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock), [Claude Platform on AWS](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-platform-on-aws), [Vertex](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/google-vertex-ai), [Foundry](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/microsoft-foundry), [LLM gateway](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway).

**Codex Supported Auth/Env Setups**

Based on current official Codex docs:

- ChatGPT account auth: `codex login`, including Plus, Pro, Business, Edu, Enterprise plans.
- CI/API-key auth: official non-interactive docs now call out `CODEX_API_KEY` for `codex exec`; Sepo currently uses `OPENAI_API_KEY`, so I would support both for compatibility.
- Codex GitHub Action: uses an `openai-api-key` input backed by a secret such as `OPENAI_API_KEY`.
- Custom/OpenAI-compatible providers: `~/.codex/config.toml` or project `.codex/config.toml` with `[model_providers.<id>]`, `base_url`, `env_key`, `wire_api`, headers, or command-backed auth.
- Azure OpenAI: Codex supports an Azure provider config using `env_key = "AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY"`, Azure base URL, `api-version` query param, and `wire_api = "responses"`. Important: `AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY` alone is not enough; Codex still needs provider config.
- Built-in Amazon Bedrock provider: `model_provider = "amazon-bedrock"` plus AWS profile/region/credential chain.
- Data residency / proxy: `openai_base_url` for the built-in OpenAI provider, or a custom provider for gateways.
- Local OSS mode: Ollama / LM Studio via `--oss` and config.

Sources: [Codex non-interactive auth](https://developers.openai.com/codex/noninteractive), [Codex config/custom providers](https://developers.openai.com/codex/config-advanced), [Codex GitHub Action](https://developers.openai.com/codex/github-action), [Codex repo README](https://github.com/openai/codex).

**Recommended Implementation**

1. Keep provider choices as `auto|codex|claude`; do not split into `claude-bedrock`, `codex-azure`, etc. Those are credential/config variants of the same CLI providers.
2. Add fixed, explicit inputs to `resolve-agent-provider` for known readiness signals:
   - Codex: `codex_api_key`, `openai_api_key`, `azure_openai_api_key`.
   - Claude: `claude_oauth_token`, `anthropic_api_key`, `anthropic_auth_token`, `anthropic_aws_api_key`, `aws_bearer_token_bedrock`, `anthropic_foundry_api_key`, plus provider activation/config vars where needed.
3. Update `resolve-provider.sh` so `auto` considers these additional signals, while keeping Codex-first behavior when both are configured.
4. Update `run-agent-task` and `run.ts` to forward the same fixed env vars to `acpx`.
5. Update workflow call sites to wire repo secrets explicitly. Do not pass arbitrary secrets wholesale.
6. Update docs and onboarding output so setup no longer says only `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`.
7. Add resolver tests for:
   - `CODEX_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY`
   - `AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY` with Codex
   - `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`
   - `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`
   - `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`
   - Bedrock / Foundry / AWS workspace API-key cases
   - deterministic Codex-first tie behavior

One design question before coding: should Sepo only detect/pass these env vars and assume provider-specific config already exists, or should Sepo also generate `.codex/config.toml` / Claude settings for cases like Azure OpenAI and gateways? My recommendation for the first PR is detection + fixed env forwarding + docs, leaving config generation for a separate issue because it has more policy/security surface.

title: More flexible api key setups for codex and claude
